incident-bot: 🔔 HIGH Embedding QPS spike detected for prod-dedicated-3 (gpu-pool-7). Error 429s rising, token cpu/gpu queue growth > 300s. AlertID: EBS-2026-03-15-01
Alex (oncall): I'm paged, jumping in. Starting triage.
Maya (runtime): seeing sustained concurrent requests from api-key org: 'quantify-inc' hitting /v1/embeddings, concurrency ~120. Dedicated pool saturating.
Jordan (sre): dashboards: https://dash.redwood/embeddings/pool7 - GPU utilization 98%, queued requests up.
Alex (oncall): Quick customer impact summary?
Lee (support): Support tickets from Quantify mention slow responses and retries, 3 customers reporting timeouts. High business impact for them.
Maya (runtime): stack: runtime queue fills because KV cache miss rate spiked (large unique prefixes). Auto-batching can't coalesce; we see small requests but massively parallel.
Sam (sdk): any temporary mitigations we can push from platform side to reduce client impact?
Alex (oncall): Propose immediate live mitigations: 1) soft per-key concurrency limit 2) temporary minute-level quota 3) enable 429 with Retry-After and clear guidance to clients 4) optionally disable the heavy model variant for this pool. Thoughts?
Jordan (sre): I'll apply soft concurrency limit at edge-shaper: set max_concurrency=16 for the offending api-key. Also set rate-limit 600/min. This will return 429+Retry-After.
Maya (runtime): I'll enable an automatic fallback to smaller-embedding model on overflow so fewer tokens per request. Rolling now to pool7 (will take ~30s).
Alex (oncall): Notify SDK/devx so customers get client guidance. @Sam can you draft quick mitigation steps we should push to the SDK and support?
Sam (sdk): On it. Draft to post here and to support -> customer. Will include: idempotency, reduced parallelism, capped retries with jitter, honoring Retry-After.
Sam (sdk): Posting suggested short guidance for customers (copy/paste):
Sam (sdk]: ```
Temporary client guidance (apply immediately):
- Reduce concurrent requests per API key to <= 10.
- Respect 429 + Retry-After headers. Backoff policy: exponential backoff with jitter, max 5 retries.
- Use idempotency keys for non-streaming requests: send header "Idempotency-Key: <uuid>".
- Batch items into larger embedding calls where possible (fewer concurrent requests).
- Reduce chunk size / max_tokens if generating content.
Example exponential backoff (python):
import time, random
for attempt in range(5):
    resp = call_embedding_api()
    if resp.status == 200:
        break
    if resp.status == 429 or resp.status >= 500:
        sleep = (2 ** attempt) + random.uniform(0, 0.5)
        time.sleep(sleep)
```
Alex (oncall): Nice. Add explicit header handling example for curl to show idempotency.
Sam (sdk): Adding curl example:
Sam (sdk]: ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: 3fa85f64-5717-4562-b3fc-2c963f66afa6" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input": ["a","b","c"], "model": "embed-lite-1"}'
```
Maya (runtime): We're also toggling a temporary heuristic to coalesce similar prefix requests in the router (experimental). Should reduce duplicate work; enabling now.
Jordan (sre): Concurrency limit applied at 2177771280. Monitoring.
QA-Bot: Canary checks: latency for embeddings decreased from 4.8s -> 2.1s after limit, error rate down from 18% -> 6% in first 60s.
Lee (support): I'll post a customer-facing note to Quantify: explain we're throttling to protect overall service, include recommended client changes and ETA for mitigation.
Alex (oncall): Handoff: I'm going offline in 20m. @Maya you'll own running mitigations and follow up with platform team. @Jordan keep observing edge-shaper metrics and if error rate >10% after 10m escalate to eng-runtime.
Maya (runtime): Ack. I'll keep the fallback model and coalescing on for now, and progressively relax limits if safe.
Sam (sdk): Final SDK guidance to push to docs & support thread (short):
Sam (sdk]: "When you see 429s, implement exponential backoff with jitter (cap retries to 5), include Idempotency-Key for request dedupe, and reduce concurrency. For streaming, prefer single stream per connection and multiplex at app layer rather than concurrent streams."
Also: we will release a small SDK patch to 0.9.7 with built-in backoff + idempotency helper. ETA 2 hours.
Jordan (sre): Observability note: add a temporary dashboard tile for per-key concurrency and per-key queue depth so we can spot next offenders quickly.
Alex (oncall): After mitigation, we should run a post-incident customer-impact assessment and consider rate-limiting defaults per plan. Create ticket for product.
Lee (support): Created ticket PRD-4521 for customer outreach and credit review.
Maya (runtime): Update: fallback to embed-lite propagated to pool7 at 2177771345, average tokens/request down 40%. Queues shrink.
Jordan (sre): After 10 minutes: 429s at 1.2%, GPU util 72%, queue depth normalizing.
Alex (oncall): Great. Next steps: 1) Sam ship SDK patch 0.9.7 with recommended backoff 2) Jordan keep the per-key limits in place for 1hr then evaluate 3) Maya follow up on router coalescing perf 4) Lee coordinate customer comms.
Sam (sdk): I'll open PR and ping eng-devex.
Maya (runtime): I'll keep monitoring and will hand back to next oncall at 2177771700 if stable.
Alex (oncall): Handoff: @Jordan you're primary after 2177771700. Please escalate to eng-runtime if error rate >5% persists.
Jordan (sre): Ack.
incident-bot: Incident EBS-2026-03-15-01 mitigations applied: soft-rate-limit, model-fallback, router-coalesce. Status: mitigated -> monitoring.
Alex (oncall): Closing my loop, good job team.
Lee (support): I'll keep Quantify updated and post the final note after the SDK patch lands. :thumbsup:
Sam (sdk): Patch queued, will update thread with release link.
Maya (runtime): Leaving coalescing on, will revert later if it causes anomalies.
Alex (oncall): Last: remember to include replay safe instructions for customers who retried incorrectly (duplicate-handling guidance).
Sam (sdk): Will add doc section on "De-dup and safe retries" in the KB.
Jordan (sre): Logging note: capture first 50 unique prefixes causing cache misses for postmortem.
Alex (oncall): Thanks all — closing thread, monitoring continues.
